articles.title: 175-Year-Old West Bengal Temple Collapses Into Ganges as Erosion Breaches Barriers
articles.excerpt: Severe riverbank erosion overwhelmed protective barriers and sandbag reinforcements around the historic structure, the second temple lost to the Ganges in less than a week.
articles.nri_angle: Heritage sites along the Ganges hold deep cultural significance for the diaspora, and the twin collapses highlight threats from environmental change.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Telangana Assembly Erupts as Speaker Breaks Down Over Alleged Caste Slurs by BRS Lawmaker
articles.excerpt: BRS MLC Tata Madhu was arrested for allegedly using derogatory language against Dalit Speaker Gaddam Prasad Kumar during a protest outside the Assembly, with CM Revanth Reddy calling it a "dark day for Telangana."
articles.nri_angle: Caste-based attacks on a constitutional officeholder challenge democratic norms that diaspora Indians regard as fundamental to India's governance.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Clears ₹1.1 Lakh Crore Defence Acquisition With 98% Sourced From Domestic Industry
articles.excerpt: The Defence Acquisition Council approved procurement proposals spanning CBRN vehicles, marine gas turbines and advanced helicopters for all three services, with nearly all sourcing from Indian manufacturers.
articles.nri_angle: The expanding Indian defence manufacturing pipeline creates potential opportunities for Indian-origin defence technology professionals abroad.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Western Powers Push to Refer Iran to UN Security Council as IAEA Warns of Nuclear Access Crisis
articles.excerpt: The US, UK, France and Germany have drafted a resolution to send Iran's nuclear file to the Security Council for the first time in two decades, as the IAEA says it has lost knowledge of Iran's enriched uranium stocks.
articles.nri_angle: Any escalation around the Strait of Hormuz could spike oil prices for Indian consumers, while US sanctions uncertainty continues to complicate India's strategic Chabahar port operations.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: UK Recognises India's Carbon Credit Scheme, Easing Carbon Tax Burden on Exporters
articles.excerpt: Britain has included India's Carbon Credit Trading Scheme in its qualifying list under the UK CBAM, allowing Indian exporters to claim relief on carbon-intensive goods shipped to the UK.
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin UK business owners importing carbon-intensive goods from India stand to benefit from lower CBAM compliance costs under the recognition.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Hosts BRICS Summit This Week With Trade, AI and Payment Systems on the Agenda
articles.excerpt: The 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi on September 12-13 will test whether the expanded 11-member bloc can turn shared interests into concrete economic cooperation.
articles.image_caption: World leaders pose for a family photograph at the 17th BRICS Summit in Rio de Janeiro in 2025. India hosts the 18th summit in New Delhi on September 12-13, 2026.
articles.nri_angle: Expanded BRICS payment linkages could reduce remittance costs and trade facilitation measures could benefit Indian-owned businesses across BRICS markets.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Punjab Police Arrest FBI Most Wanted Fraudster Who Fled U.S. Over $600,000 SNAP Scam
articles.excerpt: Manjeet Singh Bedi, a naturalized American citizen wanted for wire fraud and food benefits theft, was captured in Jalandhar after fleeing the United States through Canada.
articles.nri_angle: A naturalized American citizen of Indian origin is caught between two countries' legal systems after allegedly defrauding a U.S. federal food assistance program and fleeing to India.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Backs UN Equal Earth Map Resolution but Draws Red Line Over Kashmir Depiction
articles.excerpt: The UN General Assembly adopted the 'Correct the Map' resolution by 164-1, with India voting in favour while insisting Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh be depicted per its official map.
articles.nri_angle: The resolution could change how world maps in schools and digital platforms depict Indian territory, directly relevant to NRI families navigating representations of India abroad.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India and China Hold First Corps Commander-Level Talks in Arunachal Pradesh
articles.excerpt: Lt Gen Girish Kalia leads the Indian delegation at the Wacha-Damai border meeting point, marking the first such high-level military engagement in the eastern sector.
articles.nri_angle: Escalation or de-escalation along the India-China border directly affects regional stability and India's strategic posture, closely watched by the diaspora.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Modi Doubles Down on 'Dimagi Naxal' Rhetoric at Delhi College Centenary
articles.excerpt: Addressing students at SRCC's 100th anniversary, the prime minister compared his controversial phrase to a homeopathic remedy that forces critics to reveal themselves.
articles.image_caption: Prime Minister Narendra Modi speaking at an event. Modi reprised his 'dimagi Naxal' label at the SRCC centenary celebrations in Delhi.
articles.nri_angle: Modi's youth outreach and political messaging at elite institutions shapes the political discourse followed closely by the Indian diaspora.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Nikita Porwal Carries India's Hopes Into Miss World 2026 Finale Tonight
articles.excerpt: The Ujjain native competes for India's seventh Miss World crown at the 73rd edition in Nha Trang, Vietnam, airing live on JioHotstar at 5:30 PM IST.
articles.image_caption: Nikita Porwal, India's representative at the Miss World 2026 pageant. The Madhya Pradesh native carries India's hopes into the finale.
articles.nri_angle: Indian diaspora audiences worldwide can watch the finale live on JioHotstar and streaming platforms as Porwal competes for India's seventh Miss World crown.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Strongest El Niño in 70 Years Drives Global Food Prices to Highest Since 2022
articles.excerpt: The UN weather agency says El Niño will persist through February 2027 with near certainty, as FAO data shows food commodity prices climbing across every major category.
articles.image_caption: The strongest El Niño in 70 years is driving global food prices to their highest levels since 2022.
articles.nri_angle: India faces below-normal rainfall that threatens sugar and rice crops, while rising global food prices affect household costs for diaspora families sending remittances and for consumers worldwide.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: How a WhatsApp Group of 500 Engineers Is Guiding Nepal's Desperate Tunnel Rescue
articles.excerpt: A messaging group set up before the August 26 disaster has become an unlikely lifeline, sharing tunnel blueprints and worker locations as rescue teams search for hundreds still missing.
articles.image_caption: A WhatsApp group of over 500 engineers is providing tunnel layouts and access drawings to rescue workers at six devastated hydropower sites in Nepal.
articles.nri_angle: India is among the countries assisting Nepal's rescue operations, and the disaster highlights infrastructure vulnerabilities across South Asia's growing hydropower sector.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: SCO Summit Leaves Proposed Development Bank Unresolved as India Balances Bloc Ties
articles.excerpt: The Bishkek summit delivered institutional reforms and a 28-document package, but the proposed SCO Development Bank remains without a founding agreement, capital structure, or headquarters.
articles.image_caption: The SCO summit in Bishkek adopted 28 documents including the Bishkek Declaration but stopped short of launching the proposed Development Bank.
articles.nri_angle: India's stance on the proposed bank and connectivity projects directly shapes the economic architecture that NRIs and Indian businesses navigate across Central and South Asia.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Drops Pre-Defined OBC Lists From Census 2027, Reigniting Caste Data Debate
articles.excerpt: The government will use open-ended caste entries instead of administrative OBC classifications, drawing fierce criticism from opposition parties who warn of a repeat of the unusable 2011 data.
articles.image_caption: India's government has dropped pre-defined OBC lists from Census 2027, opting instead for open-ended text entries for caste enumeration.
articles.nri_angle: Census caste data shapes reservation policies that affect educational admissions and government employment for Indian citizens and those maintaining ties to India's social systems.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Two Workers Pulled Alive From Nepal Tunnel Nine Days After Devastating Floods
articles.excerpt: Sanjay Sah and Kabir Maharjan are the first survivors rescued from hydropower tunnels where hundreds remain trapped after the August 26 glacier collapse.
articles.image_caption: Sanjay Sah and Kabir Maharjan were pulled alive from the Upper Trishuli 3A hydropower tunnel on Friday, nine days after a glacier collapse triggered devastating floods.
articles.nri_angle: India has sent rescue experts to assist Nepal's search operations, and hundreds of foreign nationals including pilgrims and trekkers remain missing.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Publicis Wins PepsiCo's $5.4 Billion Media Account, Exits Coca-Cola Pitch
articles.excerpt: The French agency group displaces Omnicom as PepsiCo's lead global media partner in a deal covering 200-plus markets, and withdraws from rival Coca-Cola's ongoing review.
articles.image_caption: PepsiCo's global headquarters in Purchase, New York. The company awarded its 5.4 billion dollar media account to Publicis Groupe, which exited the competing Coca-Cola pitch to secure the deal.
articles.nri_angle: Publicis already handled PepsiCo's media in India and several Asian markets; the global consolidation puts Indian advertising professionals at the center of a unified 200-market operation.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Delhi Court Grants Bail to AAP's Satyendar Jain in Jal Board Corruption Case
articles.excerpt: The former Delhi water minister was ordered to furnish a personal bond of Rs 2 lakh after spending over two weeks in judicial custody on charges of manipulating sewage treatment plant tenders.
articles.image_caption: Satyendar Jain, the AAP leader, was granted bail by a Delhi court in a Jal Board corruption case.
articles.nri_angle: The case adds to the string of legal battles facing AAP leaders, a party that drew significant NRI support during its anti-corruption campaigns.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Canada Probes Import Risks After India Raid Uncovers Fake Labels on Food Products
articles.excerpt: The Canadian Food Inspection Agency is the first foreign regulator to respond after Indian authorities seized nearly $80,000 worth of relabelled PepsiCo, Nestle and Coca-Cola products from a Mumbai warehouse.
articles.image_caption: Food safety authorities inspect product labels at a facility. Canadian regulators are investigating import risks after Indian agencies uncovered fake labels on food products meant for export.
articles.nri_angle: The incident raises safety concerns for Indian diaspora communities in Canada who regularly purchase imported Indian food products.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Telangana CM Sacks Minister Konda Surekha From Cabinet Over Party Indiscipline
articles.excerpt: Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy removed the Forest and Environment minister after Congress high command backed disciplinary action triggered by her daughter's public attacks on party leadership.
articles.image_caption: Telangana Chief Minister Revanth Reddy, who dismissed minister Konda Surekha from his cabinet over party indiscipline.
articles.nri_angle: The internal Congress turmoil in Telangana is closely watched by NRIs from the state who maintain strong ties to regional politics.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Posts 7.8% GDP Growth in Q1, but Data Debate Clouds the Numbers
articles.excerpt: India's April-June growth comfortably beat forecasts, driven by an investment surge and manufacturing strength, but critics question whether a base-year revision inflated the headline figure.
articles.image_caption: The North Block in New Delhi houses India's Ministry of Finance. India reported 7.8 percent GDP growth in the first quarter, though economists questioned the methodology behind the numbers.
articles.nri_angle: India's GDP credibility debate affects NRI equity investments, rupee-denominated assets, and global capital allocation to Indian markets.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Apple Maps Adopts 'Lake America' as MapQuest Soars to No. 1 App
articles.excerpt: Apple followed Google in renaming Lake Ontario after Trump's executive order, while MapQuest's refusal to comply made it the top free iPhone app in the US.
articles.image_caption: The Apple Maps application. Apple Maps briefly displayed the Gulf of Mexico as 'Lake America' following the federal name change, while MapQuest surged to the number one spot on the App Store.
articles.nri_angle: The renaming of Lake Ontario affects the millions of Indian-origin residents in the US and Canada, two of the largest diaspora populations, amid an escalating trade war between the two countries.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Nepal PM Balen Shah Thanks India for Flood Aid as Death Toll Passes 1,100
articles.excerpt: In his first parliamentary address on the crisis, Nepal's prime minister detailed the government's response and praised India's assistance including DNA testing support as nearly 4,000 people remain missing.
articles.image_caption: Nepal Prime Minister Balen Shah. Shah publicly thanked India for flood relief as the death toll from devastating floods crossed 1,100.
articles.nri_angle: Over 100 Indian nationals and 37 NRIs were among those missing in the floods, and India's rapid humanitarian response including DNA testing reflects deep bilateral ties.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Google Escapes Ad Tech Breakup as Judge Rejects DOJ Forced Sale
articles.excerpt: Federal judge opts for behavioral remedies over structural separation, marking the third consecutive failure by U.S. antitrust enforcers to break up a major tech company.
articles.image_caption: The Googleplex, Google's corporate headquarters in Mountain View, California. A federal judge rejected the DOJ's demand that Google sell off its ad technology business.
articles.nri_angle: The ruling affects the broader tech industry where many Indian-origin professionals work, and has implications for digital advertising costs that impact Indian-American small business owners.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Modi Demands End to Terror Double Standards at SCO Summit in Bishkek
articles.excerpt: At the 26th SCO Summit in Kyrgyzstan, PM Modi called for dismantling the entire ecosystem of terrorism while sharing warm exchanges with Xi Jinping and Putin — as Pakistan's Sharif stood by without interaction.
articles.image_caption: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi at the SCO Summit. Modi called on member states to end double standards on terrorism and pushed for greater counter-terror cooperation.
articles.nri_angle: India's anti-terrorism stance and frozen India-Pakistan ties directly affect diaspora communities through visa policies, security postures, and bilateral relations.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Both Parents' Vitamin B12 Levels Linked to Birth Defect Risk, Major Study Finds
articles.excerpt: A large prospective study from China shows that higher B12 in fathers — not just mothers — before conception is associated with fewer birth defects, a finding with outsized implications for India's B12-deficient population.
articles.image_caption: An expectant couple during pregnancy. A large prospective study found that higher vitamin B12 levels in both parents before conception are linked to a lower risk of birth defects.
articles.nri_angle: Vitamin B12 deficiency affects an estimated 40–75% of India's population, making these findings directly relevant to Indian families planning pregnancies — especially those on vegetarian diets.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Centre Defers Manipur Census Amid Protests Over NRC and Ethnic Tensions
articles.excerpt: The September 1 house-listing exercise was put on hold after Amit Shah chaired a review and civil-society groups demanded an NRC update first.
articles.nri_angle: Diaspora members from Manipur face continued uncertainty as institutional governance stalls in the state.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Three Killed in Armed Attack on Manipur Village as Naga-Kuki Violence Escalates
articles.excerpt: Suspected militants opened fire on a Kuki-inhabited village in Kangpokpi, killing three and critically injuring four.
articles.nri_angle: Ongoing ethnic violence in Manipur remains a concern for diaspora families with roots in the northeastern state.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
